summary: The test suite (183 tests, all passing in ~19s) is real but badly skewed: it deeply covers pure string helpers and a few mocked stage flows while leaving the delivery-critical surfaces — observe.py (2,768 lines, 16 endpoints), pipeline wiring, CLI/SIGTERM, resume semantics, the PDF build, and most of the router fallback matrix — at zero coverage, and one stage test silently makes live HTTP calls to Wikipedia/PyPI/arXiv/OpenAlex. Delivery infrastructure is essentially absent for the stated production goal: the checked-in docker-compose.yml is a dead artifact from the doc-expand era (services the README itself rejects, `build: .` with no Dockerfile), the wheel is not actually installable because config.yaml/models.yaml are CWD-relative and not packaged, there is no CI, no release process, and — most importantly for a product whose deliverable is generated text — no output-quality eval harness of any kind.
strengths: 183 tests pass deterministically in 19s with no external test runner config needed (pytest settings in pyproject.toml, asyncio_mode=auto); LLM calls in stage tests are properly mocked via AsyncMock routers so no test depends on API keys.

Several tests encode real, specific past regressions rather than padding: tests/test_base.py:242-290 pins the geminicli _PROBED_UNAVAILABLE key-mismatch fix (commit fd18d6e), the _instructor_mode matrix (test_base.py:361-394) pins the Mistral/Groq/Gemini JSON-mode workarounds, and test_base.py:101-112 covers Anthropic cache_control blocks in _msg_chars.

Stage tests consistently verify the two invariants that matter for resume: skip-when-complete idempotency (s4_audit, s5_research, s7_synthesize, s8_verify, s10_assemble each have one) and per-domain failure isolation (tests/test_s3_integration.py:272-336, tests/test_s4_research.py:178).
tests/test_bibliography.py uses pytest-httpx (httpx_mock) correctly for hermetic Semantic Scholar API tests — the right pattern exists in the repo, it just isn't applied everywhere.

uv.lock is checked in (reproducible dev environment), the console entry point (know-expand = know_expand.cli:main) works, .gitignore correctly excludes .env and runs/, and the project LICENSE is MIT with an all-permissive dependency tree (docling/spacy/litellm/instructor/langgraph MIT, sentence-transformers Apache-2.0, pypdf/httpx BSD) — no copyleft contamination.

issues.title: Package is not actually pip-installable: config files are CWD-relative and not shipped in the wheel
issues.detail: know_expand/config.py:116-121 defaults load_config() to Path("config.yaml") / Path("models.yaml") resolved against the current working directory, and know_expand/cli.py:159 calls load_config() with no arguments. config.yaml and models.yaml live at the repo root, outside the know_expand package, so the hatchling wheel (pyproject.toml:1-3) will not include them. Result: `pip install know-expand && know-expand paper.pdf` fails with FileNotFoundError from any directory except a repo checkout. Compounding this, LlamaCppConfig hardcodes a private LAN IP as the library default (know_expand/config.py:70: base_url="http://192.168.1.117:8080") — a personal-machine artifact baked into shipped defaults. For a product 'many users run', the entry point only works for the author.

issues.title: docker-compose.yml is a dead artifact from the doc-expand era; README documents a different, also-nonexistent deployment
issues.detail: docker-compose.yml:1-35 defines grobid, anystyle, and phoenix services — zero references to any of them exist in know_expand/ or config.yaml (verified by grep), and README.md:889 explicitly lists 'Phoenix/Langfuse as Docker service' as a rejected alternative. The compose network is still named doc_expand (docker-compose.yml:7, pre-rename), the app service uses `build: .` but there is no Dockerfile anywhere in the repo, and the volumes (./state, ./output, docker-compose.yml:47-49) do not match the actual runs/{run_id}/state|logs|output layout. Meanwhile README.md:774-809 shows a *different* compose file (app + ollama profile) that is not the one checked in and equally cannot work without a Dockerfile. The entire documented Deployment section is fiction; `docker compose up` fails immediately. README.md:765 also instructs `cp .env.example .env` but no .env.example exists in the repo.

issues.title: Test suite is not hermetic: s4_audit integration tests make live HTTP calls to OpenAlex/Wikipedia/PyPI/arXiv
issues.detail: tests/test_s3_integration.py:186-189 and 309-314 patch fetch_anchors/fetch_bibliography/fetch_anchor_neighbors/make_router but NOT fetch_sources_for_terms, which s4_audit.run() invokes unconditionally (know_expand/stages/s4_audit.py:232,251). Every test run issues real network requests for the fixture terms 'Alpha'/'Beta'/'Gamma'. The suite only passes offline because sources.py swallows every exception into debug logs (know_expand/sources.py:292-294, 346-348) — i.e., the network dependency is masked, not absent. Smoking gun: the observed RuntimeWarning during the run ('AsyncLimiter instance is being re-used across loops' at know_expand/sources.py:314) proves _fetch_openalex_works executed inside the 'fully mocked' test. That warning also exposes a latent production bug: the module-level cached _OPENALEX_LIMITER (sources.py:40-46) is reused across event loops, which aiolimiter documents as undefined behavior — relevant the moment multiple runs share a process.

issues.title: No CI/CD, no lint, no type-check, no coverage measurement — quality gates do not exist
issues.detail: There is no .github/ directory (verified), no workflow files, no Makefile/tox/nox, and the dev extra (pyproject.toml:39-44) contains only pytest, pytest-asyncio, and pytest-httpx — no ruff, no mypy, no pytest-cov, despite .gitignore:211 listing .ruff_cache/ (tooling was apparently used ad hoc and never committed as config). Nothing runs the 183 tests automatically; the commit message claiming '182 tests' (3df1514) is already stale (183 collected), which is exactly the drift CI would catch. For a multi-user product, every merge to main is currently unverified.

issues.title: The product's actual deliverable — generated long-form text and a PDF — has zero quality evaluation
issues.detail: The value of know-expand is the quality of LLM-generated research prose, citations, and the assembled PDF. None of that is evaluated anywhere: there is no eval harness, no golden input document with expected-output regression, no rubric/LLM-judge scoring, no citation-accuracy benchmark, and no fixtures directory (verified by find). All LLM interactions in tests are canned Pydantic objects (e.g. tests/test_s4_research.py:38-63), so prompt changes — the highest-churn, highest-risk surface, e.g. the 1,017-line s5_research.py — can silently degrade output with no signal. Even the deterministic end of delivery is untested: the pandoc + double-xelatex path (a 'non-negotiable' invariant per CLAUDE.md) is only exercised via its skip branch (tests/test_s7_assemble.py:165 test_s7_pdf_skip_when_pandoc_unavailable); no test ever produces a PDF. A judgment that 'the build is green' currently says nothing about whether the product output got better or worse.

issues.title: Coverage is heavily skewed: 38% of all tests target two string helpers while observe.py, pipeline.py, cli.py, and 6 of 11 stages have zero tests
issues.detail: tests/test_s10_pdf.py contains 70 of the 183 tests (38%), all for _fix_bare_math and _sanitize_bib_entry — two pure string functions in s10_assemble. Meanwhile: observe.py (2,768 lines — 24% of the codebase — 16 HTTP endpoints, the qa/taxonomy IPC protocol, SIGCHLD handling, subprocess spawning) has zero tests; pipeline.py (LangGraph wiring), cli.py (including the SIGTERM-emits-run_stopped invariant listed in CLAUDE.md's 'Important constraints'), and state.py's emit() are untested; stages s0_ingest, s1_assess (interview IPC), s2_extract, s3_graph (taxonomy review IPC), s6_align, and s9_prereq have no tests at all. The router fallback matrix documented in CLAUDE.md has 5 rows but tests cover only 3 — the Retry-After exact-sleep path, the headerless 429 exponential backoff (2s/4s/8s), and the 3-consecutive-failures permanent skip (know_expand/agents/base.py:726-930, notably duplicated in two near-identical copies) are all untested. The two human-in-the-loop IPC protocols and the resume mechanism — the features most likely to break under concurrent multi-user load — are precisely the untested ones.

issues.title: Undeclared direct runtime dependencies: PyYAML and langchain-core
issues.detail: know_expand/config.py:4 does `import yaml` and know_expand/agents/lc_adapter.py:17-26 imports langchain_core directly, but pyproject.toml:9-34 declares neither PyYAML nor langchain-core. Both currently resolve only transitively (via litellm/docling and langgraph respectively). A routine upstream dependency refactor would break a fresh install of this package with ImportError at startup — config loading is the first thing cli.py does. This is exactly the class of breakage a lockfile does not protect end users from, since pip consumers install from pyproject metadata, not uv.lock.

issues.title: Every stage test file is named for the pre-rename stage numbering — systematic off-by-rename drift
issues.detail: After the stage renumbering (audit inserted at S4, etc.), no test file was renamed: tests/test_s3_integration.py tests s4_audit (its own docstring at line 2 still says 'Stage 3 (Anchored Audit)' while line 218-219 asserts stages['4']), test_s4_research.py tests s5_research, test_s5_synthesize.py tests s7_synthesize, test_s6_verify.py tests s8_verify, and test_s7_assemble.py/test_s10_pdf.py test s10_assemble. Function names compound it (test_s3_run_writes_outputs..., test_s4_writes_section..., test_s6_detects_needs_citation for s8_verify). Anyone triaging a failure in 'test_s6_verify' will open s6_align.py first. Pure rename debt, but it makes the suite actively misleading and CI failure output unreadable.

issues.title: No release/versioning machinery: 0.1.0 forever, no tags, no changelog, bare project metadata
issues.detail: pyproject.toml:7 pins version="0.1.0" across all 64 commits; the repo has zero git tags (verified), no CHANGELOG, and know_expand/__init__.py carries no __version__. The [project] table omits license, readme, classifiers, urls, and description even though a LICENSE file (MIT) and a 59KB README exist — so a published wheel would surface as anonymous metadata on PyPI. System-level runtime requirements are also undeclared and unenforced: spacy's en_core_web_sm (a hard constraint per CLAUDE.md) appears nowhere in pyproject or uv.lock, and pandoc/xelatex/node(npx for geminicli) have no preflight documentation beyond prose. A new user's first run fails on a missing spaCy model with no install-time hint.

issues.title: Delivery infrastructure assumes a single developer machine, contradicting the multi-user production goal
issues.detail: Everything in the delivery layer is single-tenant: config resolution from CWD (config.py:116-121), runs/ rooted in the repo directory, the serve process is documented (README.md:828) as the sole observability surface with no auth/health-check/container story, and the cheapest model tier (geminicli) depends on a personal OAuth token at ~/.gemini/oauth_creds.json driving the free gemini-cli quota — per-developer-machine state that cannot be shipped to concurrent users and is at best ToS-grey for a hosted product (per-user personal quota repurposed as product capacity). There is no horizontal story at all: no image, no process supervisor, no queue, no per-tenant isolation of runs/. For SaaS or even serious self-hosting, the delivery architecture has to be designed, not patched.

production_gaps: No Dockerfile and no working container path — the checked-in docker-compose.yml cannot start (references a Dockerfile that does not exist and services from the abandoned doc-expand architecture); README's Deployment section describes a compose file that is not in the repo.
No CI pipeline of any kind (.github/ absent): tests, lint, type-check, and packaging are never verified automatically; no coverage measurement exists so the severe coverage skew is invisible.

No output-quality eval harness: no golden documents, no citation-accuracy or hallucination regression checks, no LLM-judge or rubric scoring — prompt changes ship blind even though generated text is the entire product.

Wheel is broken for end users: config.yaml/models.yaml are not packaged and are resolved relative to CWD, so the installed console script only works from a repo checkout; PyYAML and langchain-core are undeclared dependencies.

System dependencies unmanaged: spaCy en_core_web_sm, pandoc, xelatex, and node/npx (for geminicli) are required at runtime but appear in no dependency metadata, preflight check at install time, or container image.

Tests issue live third-party HTTP requests (OpenAlex/Wikipedia/PyPI/arXiv) from the 'mocked' s4_audit integration tests — flaky offline/air-gapped and rude to upstream APIs under CI parallelism; no network-isolation marker or socket-blocking fixture.
No release process: version frozen at 0.1.0, zero git tags, no CHANGELOG, no PyPI metadata (license/classifiers/urls/readme undeclared); referenced .env.example file does not exist.

No load or concurrency testing for the serve process and its file-based IPC (qa_queue.jsonl, taxonomy_choice.json, pipeline_pid) despite the goal of many concurrent users; observe.py's 16 endpoints have zero tests of any kind.

verdicts.title: Package is not actually pip-installable: config files are CWD-relative and not shipped in the wheel
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual assertion was verified by reading the code and reproduced empirically. (1) know_expand/config.py:116-118 defaults load_config() to CWD-relative Path("config.yaml")/Path("models.yaml") and reads them with no fallback; cli.py:159 calls load_config() with no args. (2) config.yaml and models.yaml live at the repo root, outside the know_expand package. (3) Built the wheel with `uv build --wheel` under the hatchling backend (pyproject.toml has no [tool.hatch.build], force-include, or MANIFEST.in): the wheel contains 31 files and zero yaml files. (4) Reproduced the exact failure: importing load_config() and calling it from /tmp raises FileNotFoundError: 'config.yaml'. (5) config.py:70 hardcodes base_url="http://192.168.1.117:8080" (a private LAN IP), duplicated in config.yaml:67. No mitigating code exists anywhere: no __file__-relative resolution, no importlib.resources, no env-var override, and observe.py's _spawn_pipeline passes no cwd= to Popen, so even the web-UI spawn path inherits the CWD dependency. The only soft spots are framing, not substance: pip install itself succeeds (execution fails from any CWD other than the repo root — including repo subdirectories, marginally worse than claimed), the llamacpp IP degrades silently via probe_models() health-check rather than crashing, and the package appears unpublished with a README documenting only the repo-checkout uv workflow, which tempers today's real-world impact. None of these refute the claim's core: an installed wheel's entry point cannot run outside a repo checkout root.

verdicts.title: docker-compose.yml is a dead artifact from the doc-expand era; README documents a different, also-nonexistent deployment
verdicts.reasoning: Every factual assertion verified against the repo. (1) docker-compose.yml defines grobid (line 2), anystyle (line 14), and phoenix (line 26); case-insensitive grep for these names across know_expand/, config.yaml, models.yaml, pyproject.toml, and tests/ returns zero matches, and grep for their ports (8070/4567/6006) also returns zero matches — the code never references these services. (2) README.md:889 explicitly rejects 'Phoenix/Langfuse as Docker service' as an alternative, contradicting the checked-in compose. (3) The compose network is still named doc_expand (lines 7, 53), a pre-rename leftover; git log shows the file was last touched in early commit afb69c8 and never updated through the doc-expand → know-expand rename. (4) The app service uses `build: .` (line 38) but `find` confirms no Dockerfile or .dockerignore anywhere in the repo, so `docker compose up` fails at build. (5) Volumes ./state and ./output (lines 47-49) do not match the actual runs/{run_id}/state|logs|output layout. (6) README.md:776-800 shows a different compose file (app + ollama profile, ./runs and ./input volumes) that is not the checked-in one and also depends on the nonexistent Dockerfile. (7) README.md:765 instructs `cp .env.example .env` but no .env.example exists anywhere in the repo. No mitigating code or files found. Minor caveat: 'critical' severity is arguably a notch high since the primary uv-based run path is unaffected — this is dead deployment config plus a fictional Deployment doc section, not a defect in executing pipeline code — but the claim's substance is materially correct in every verifiable detail.

verdicts.title: Test suite is not hermetic: s4_audit integration tests make live HTTP calls to OpenAlex/Wikipedia/PyPI/arXiv
verdicts.reasoning: Attempted refutation failed; the claim verified at every load-bearing point, both structurally and empirically. (1) tests/test_s3_integration.py:185-190 and 309-314 patch only fetch_anchors/fetch_bibliography/fetch_anchor_neighbors/make_router; fetch_sources_for_terms is never patched, and there is no conftest.py or network-blocking plugin (no pytest-socket/respx/responses anywhere in the repo). (2) s4_audit.run() builds a real httpx.AsyncClient (s4_audit.py:410) and _process_domain lazily imports (line 232) and awaits fetch_sources_for_terms (line 251); the test fixtures guarantee the guards pass (fresh tmpdir so no sources cache; nodes have core/supporting centrality). (3) Ran the suite: 3 passed, and the test-run debug logs contain live HTTP responses from en.wikipedia.org — "wikipedia search failed for 'Alpha': Client error '403 Forbidden' for url 'https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=opensearch&search=Alpha...'" (same for Beta/Gamma) — real network requests issued and their failures swallowed to debug logs exactly at the cited lines (sources.py 183-184, 292-294, 346-348), which is why the suite passes regardless of connectivity: masked, not absent. (4) The cited RuntimeWarning reproduced verbatim at know_expand/sources.py:314 during test_s3_domain_failure_does_not_abort_other_domains, proving _fetch_openalex_works ran inside the "mocked" test and that the module-cached _OPENALEX_LIMITER (sources.py:40-47) created in one test's event loop was reused in another loop. (5) The latent-bug portion is corroborated in-repo: bibliography.py:70 reset_ss_limiter() exists for the identical cross-loop problem with the SS limiter and is called at s4_audit.run() start (line 376), but no reset exists for _OPENALEX_LIMITER. Severity "high" is defensible: every suite run hits public third-party APIs, and total breakage of the sources feature would be invisible to tests.
verdicts.correction: Three immaterial overstatements: "invokes unconditionally" — the call is actually guarded by `if not sources_cache.exists()` and a non-empty terms list (plus try/except), though both guards always pass under the test fixtures so the effect in tests is as claimed; the title's "PyPI/arXiv" — with no terms.json in the fixtures all terms default to term_type "academic", so only Wikipedia and OpenAlex endpoints are actually hit by these tests (PyPI/arXiv paths are reachable in general but not exercised here); and "every test run" — test_s3_skips_completed_stage individually makes no network calls (early return), though every run of the file as a whole does.

verdicts.title: No CI/CD, no lint, no type-check, no coverage measurement — quality gates do not exist
verdicts.reasoning: Every checkable assertion holds. /Users/cyan/ccr/know-expand has no .github/ directory, no workflow files, and no Makefile/tox.ini/noxfile.py/.pre-commit-config.yaml/justfile, nor any alternative CI config (CircleCI, Jenkins, Azure, Drone, Buildkite, Bitbucket). pyproject.toml lines 39-44 contain exactly pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-httpx; grep for ruff/mypy/pytest-cov/coverage across pyproject.toml and uv.lock returns zero matches, so lint/type-check/coverage tooling is absent even as locked dependencies. .gitignore line 211 is `.ruff_cache/` as cited. The drift example is real: commit 3df1514's message says "182 passing tests" while `pytest --collect-only` reports 183 collected. No mitigating automation exists anywhere: .git/hooks has only samples, .claude/settings.local.json contains no hooks, and docker-compose.yml defines runtime services (grobid/anystyle/phoenix), not test or lint runners. Two immaterial caveats: (1) the aside that ruff "was apparently used ad hoc" is probably wrong — the .ruff_cache/ entry, its "# Ruff stuff:" comment, .pypirc, and tempCodeRunnerFile.py are verbatim from the stock GitHub Python .gitignore template, i.e. boilerplate rather than evidence of prior ruff use; (2) "multi-user product" overstates a single-developer local CLI/dashboard, so the high severity is contextually aggressive though the factual gap (zero quality gates) is total. Neither caveat undermines the material claim.

verdicts.title: The product's actual deliverable — generated long-form text and a PDF — has zero quality evaluation
verdicts.reasoning: Every checkable fact in the claim is accurate. (1) /Users/cyan/ccr/know-expand/tests/test_s4_research.py:38-63 contains exactly the cited canned Pydantic factories (_make_domain_summary returning DomainSummary, _make_critique_accept returning CritiqueResult); all tests in the file patch make_router with AsyncMock, so no LLM interaction is ever exercised. (2) /Users/cyan/ccr/know-expand/tests/test_s7_assemble.py:165 is test_s7_pdf_skip_when_pandoc_unavailable, which patches shutil.which to None; the only other PDF test uses no_pdf=True. Both assert expanded.pdf does NOT exist. No test in the repo invokes pandoc or xelatex and no test ever produces a PDF, so the 'two xelatex passes' invariant from CLAUDE.md is exercised only via skip branches. (3) s5_research.py is exactly 1,017 lines. (4) find/grep confirm there is no fixtures/, evals/, or benchmarks/ directory, no golden input documents, no rubric/LLM-judge scoring code, no eval dependencies (deepeval/ragas/promptfoo absent; langsmith is only a transitive lock-file dependency, never imported), and no CI workflows at all. Even test_s3_integration.py mocks both Semantic Scholar and router.call. Mitigations were searched for and do not refute: the pipeline has runtime self-checks (S5 adversarial critic loop; S8 structural citation audit plus LLM contradiction classifier in s8_verify.py), but those are per-run product features whose LLM parts are themselves mocked in tests — they provide zero regression signal when prompts change. Severity 'high' is proportionate for a product whose entire deliverable is LLM-generated prose plus a PDF. Two marginal overstatements, neither material: the title's 'zero quality evaluation' ignores the runtime S8 structural citation audit (which IS unit-tested, in test_s6_verify.py, but only checks citation keys exist in the bibliography — not prose quality or citation accuracy); and 'even the deterministic end of delivery is untested' overlooks test_s10_pdf.py, which thoroughly unit-tests two deterministic PDF-path helpers (_fix_bare_math, _sanitize_bib_entry) — though the actual pandoc+xelatex build path indeed never runs in any test.
verdicts.correction: Two minor nuances, not refutations: (a) the deterministic helpers feeding the PDF path (_fix_bare_math, _sanitize_bib_entry in s10_assemble.py) are extensively unit-tested in tests/test_s10_pdf.py — it is specifically the pandoc + double-xelatex invocation that is never executed by any test; (b) the pipeline contains runtime quality mechanisms (S5 critic loop, S8 citation audit), but these are per-run features, not a dev-time eval/regression harness, and their LLM components are mocked in tests.

verdicts.title: Coverage is heavily skewed: 38% of all tests target two string helpers while observe.py, pipeline.py, cli.py, and 6 of 11 stages have zero tests
verdicts.reasoning: The core claim is materially correct and verified against the repo. (1) tests/ contains exactly 183 test functions; tests/test_s10_pdf.py has exactly 70 (38.3%), and its only project import is `from know_expand.stages.s10_assemble import _fix_bare_math, _sanitize_bib_entry` — both pure string functions. (2) observe.py is 2,768 of 11,412 package lines (24.3%) and no test imports it. (3) No test imports know_expand.pipeline or know_expand.cli; the SIGTERM-emits-run_stopped invariant is untested; tests import only new_run_id/setup_logging from state.py and never assert on emit() output or events.jsonl. (4) Test filenames are off-by-one from stage modules (test_s3_integration.py actually tests s4_audit, test_s7_assemble.py tests s10_assemble, etc.); the tested stage modules are s4/s5/s7/s8/s10, leaving exactly s0_ingest, s1_assess, s2_extract, s3_graph, s6_align, s9_prereq with zero stage-level tests — including both human-in-the-loop IPC protocols. (5) test_base.py covers only 3 of the 5 CLAUDE.md router fallback rows (auth-error skip, geminicli skip, all-exhausted raise); zero tests reference retry-after, _BURST_BACKOFF ([2,4,8] at base.py:376), or _fail_counts, so the Retry-After sleep, exponential backoff, and 3-consecutive-failure skip paths are untested. (6) The duplication is real: call() (base.py:735-821) and call_with_tools() (base.py:824-956) contain near-identical ~60-line error-handling blocks. However, two sub-claims are wrong, hence partial: the endpoint count and the resume-mechanism assertion (see correction). Severity 'high' for an execution-layer audit is defensible given the untested 2,768-line server and IPC protocols.
verdicts.correction: Two details are overstated. First, observe.py has 13 API endpoints (8 GET handlers at observe.py:2625-2672, 5 POST at 2688-2748), or 14 counting the root HTML page — not 16. Second, the resume mechanism is NOT entirely untested: CLAUDE.md defines resume as pipeline.json stage markers, and the marker-based skip is directly tested in five places (test_s3_integration.py::test_s3_skips_completed_stage plus test_s4/s5/s6/s7 *_idempotent_when_complete tests). What lacks coverage is the web-UI Resume button path and pipeline.py-level orchestration, not the core stage-skip mechanism. Additionally, a minor mitigation: while s2_extract has no stage-level tests, its core algorithms (union_find.py, centrality.py) have 14 dedicated tests.

verdicts.title: Undeclared direct runtime dependencies: PyYAML and langchain-core
verdicts.reasoning: The raw facts are accurate: pyproject.toml (deps lines 9-34) declares neither pyyaml nor langchain-core; know_expand/config.py:4 does a bare `import yaml` (used via yaml.safe_load at lines 120-121) and cli.py:10 imports know_expand.config at module level, so PyYAML truly is an undeclared direct dependency on the startup path; lc_adapter.py:17-26 does import langchain_core at module top. No other dependency declaration exists (no requirements.txt, no tool.uv deps). However, the impact analysis is substantially overstated. (1) lc_adapter.py is dead code: a repo-wide grep finds zero imports/references to it in cli.py, pipeline.py, any stage, the empty agents/__init__.py, or any test file — its langchain_core imports are never executed, so they cannot cause ImportError at startup or runtime. (2) langchain-core is required by langgraph's own package metadata (confirmed in uv.lock: langgraph, langgraph-checkpoint, langgraph-prebuilt all list it), and langgraph IS declared, so pip consumers get langchain-core regardless. (3) The pyyaml chain is misattributed: litellm does NOT depend on pyyaml; it arrives via seven independent transitive providers (docling-core, huggingface-hub, transformers, omegaconf, rapidocr, accelerate, langchain-core), so the 'routine upstream refactor breaks fresh install' scenario requires all of these to drop PyYAML at once — implausible. The packaging hygiene defect is real and the pyyaml fix is warranted, but severity is low/medium, not high.
verdicts.correction: PyYAML is genuinely an undeclared direct dependency on the startup path and should be added to pyproject.toml, but it resolves through seven independent transitive providers (docling-core, huggingface-hub, transformers, omegaconf, rapidocr, accelerate, langchain-core), not litellm, making the breakage scenario remote. The langchain-core half of the finding has no runtime impact at all: lc_adapter.py is never imported anywhere in the codebase (dead code), and langchain-core is pulled in by the declared langgraph dependency's own metadata anyway. Correct severity is low-to-medium packaging hygiene, not high.
